issue.title: Define the data model and storage for albums, years and rankings
issue.body:
Create the stored shapes and the storage layer the rest of the app reads and writes: albums, artists, per-year placements, matchups and decade lists. Follows the data model outline in the MVP spec (#2) and the scaffold (#3).

## Today
No code or storage exists. The spreadsheet's model, from the MVP spec (#2): one row per album with artist, year, decade, a rank (1 to 10), an honorable mention flag or neither (81 "listed only" rows), and a decade top 25 rank.

## Scope
- Define the entities in the spec's data model outline:
  - **Artist**: name, catalog id (nullable).
  - **Album**: title, artist, catalog id (nullable for manual albums), original release year (nullable), cover art URL (nullable).
  - **Year entry**: album, year, placement (`ranked`, `honorable_mention` or `listed`), rank 1 to 10 when ranked.
  - **Matchup**: album A, album B, result (`a`, `b` or `tie`), created at.
  - **Decade list entry**: decade, album, position 1 to 25, unique per decade. No candidate flag.
  - **Import review item**: the source row's text (title, artist, year, placement), candidate matches, status. Deleted once resolved.
- Store only inputs. Ratings and artist scores are computed from year entries and matchups, never stored.
- Support manual albums (no catalog id) and linking one to a catalog album later, keeping its year entry, matchups and decade list entries.
- Add migrations or an equivalent schema setup on one SQLite file, and a small data access layer with tests.
- Enforce the spec's rules:
  - An album has at most one year entry.
  - Ranks are unique within a year.
  - Honorable mention and listed entries have no order.
  - A decade list entry's album must have a year entry in that decade.
  - Undo deletes the newest matchup row.
  - Deleting an album deletes its matchups.
- The album's year is the year of its year entry, set by the user. The catalog's original release year is stored and is only the default when a row or result has no year. This settles the year question.

## Acceptance
- Tests create, read, update and delete a year entry and reject a second year entry for the same album and a duplicate rank in a year.
- Tests cover the three placements, manual album linking, matchup insert and undo, and the decade list rules.
- Schema setup runs from a clean checkout with the README steps.

## Out of scope
- Catalog search and cover art fetching (separate ticket).
- The Elo math and matchup picking (the Elo engine ticket).
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: Epic: Album ranker MVP
issue.body:
Replace the "Best Albums" spreadsheet with an app where the user searches an album catalog, ranks favorites per year with cover art, and gets artist and decade lists from Elo ratings built from yearly ranks and head-to-head matchups. The requirements are settled in #2; the other tickets build what it describes.

This epic is a container. The team builds its child tickets, not the epic itself.

## Tickets

* #2 Write the MVP requirements spec for the album ranking app (first; the build tickets follow it)
* #3 Choose the tech stack and scaffold the app
* #4 Define the data model and storage for albums, years and rankings
* #5 Add album catalog search with cover art
* #6 Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
* #7 Build the Elo rating engine and matchup screen
* #8 Add artist views by decade and overall
* #9 Add decade top 25 album lists
* #10 Import the existing spreadsheet
* #14 Deploy the app to AWS with staging and production behind a password gate

issue.title: docs: ALBUM-2 MVP requirements spec
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds the MVP requirements spec for the album ranker: one-person web app, SQLite, catalog search with covers, per-year ranking screen, head-to-head Elo ratings (single algorithm, seeded from the yearly ranks), artist and decade views, and a one-off spreadsheet import. The spec also records what the real `Best Albums.xlsx` formulas say, which differs from the ticket's description (752 rows, 81 listed-only rows, the year weight formula, two artist rollup rules).

Ticket: ALBUM-2 (https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/2)
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-album-ranker-mvp.md`

Closes #2

## Changes

- New spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-album-ranker-mvp.md`. No code.

Context size: pass skipped (not collective-wisdom)

## Proof

- **Spec committed and approved**: spec is on this branch. The user approved it in the Chief of Staff thread ("approve 2") after the Elo revision at commit 3091b45.
  After that approval, code review fixes amended the spec (rules the approved version left undefined, no change of direction): replay tiebreaks, skipped matchups, decade list upkeep, import conflict and re-run rules, the rank-plus-honorable-mention row imported as an honorable mention without a review item, and listed albums showing no rating. The merge approval covers them.
- **Every Scope item has an answer or an open question**: users and shape (§ Users and shape), MVP features, scoring (§ Scoring: head-to-head Elo), decade top 25, albums versus releases, data model outline, non-goals, calls I made, and whole-MVP acceptance each have a section; unresolved items are in § Open questions for the user.

Not proven:
- Follow-up tickets #3 to #10 still match the spec: a ticket child may only change its own ticket, so the spec's § Follow-up tickets: changes needed lists the edits for the Chief of Staff or the user to apply.

issue.title: feat: ALBUM-3 choose the stack and scaffold the app
issue.body:
Closes #3 Ticket: [ALBUM-3](https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/3). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-album-3-stack-scaffold.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-album-3-stack-scaffold.md`. ## What this does Picks the stack (TypeScript, Next.js App Router, npm, Vitest, ESLint) and commits a runnable empty scaffold: one blank home page, a config module that reads `DATABASE_PATH` from the environment, two test files, and the stack doc. `docs/agents/project.md` now has real Test, Lint and Typecheck commands and an Areas list. ## Proof - **Fresh clone runs the app and the tests**: README "Run the app" steps; `npm run dev` served `/` with `

Album ranker

` (curl on a spare port, stopped afterwards). A fresh clone of this branch passed `npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`. ``` $ npm test Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 5 passed (5) $ npm run lint (no errors) $ npm run typecheck (no errors) $ npm run build Route (app) ┌ ○ / └ ○ /_not-found ``` - **`project.md` has real Test, Lint and Typecheck values**: `docs/agents/project.md` § Commands rows are `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`; § Areas and labels lists `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`. - **Stack choice written down with the reason**: `docs/stack.md`. - **No secret, `.env` or database file committed**: `git ls-files | grep -E '\.env$|^data/|\.db$'` prints nothing; `.gitignore` covers `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `data/`, `*.db`, `*.sqlite*`.
